blocks.title: Compliance Reporting and Monitoring exam shortcuts
items: Report stays inside the company → INTERNAL REPORTING
Internal reports support management, audit, and remediation decisions.
Example: Compliance dashboard is sent to executives.
Report must go to regulator or customer → EXTERNAL REPORTING
External reporting satisfies outside obligations.
Example: Required compliance evidence is sent to a regulator.
Question asks 'Did we investigate the risk?' → DUE DILIGENCE
Due diligence is about investigation and understanding before acting.
Example: Review a vendor's security posture before contracting.
Question asks 'Did we take reasonable protective action?' → DUE CARE
Due care is about acting appropriately after risks are known.
Example: Apply controls after discovering a known vulnerability.
Formal certification statement → ATTESTATION
Attestation is stronger than simple acknowledgement.
Example: Executive formally certifies that controls are operating.
Employee confirms they read the policy → ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
Acknowledgement means receipt or understanding.
Example: User clicks 'I acknowledge' after reading the AUP.
Continuous evidence collection → AUTOMATION
Automation can reduce manual compliance work and provide ongoing evidence.
Example: Tool continuously checks encryption settings.
blocks.example: Focus on whether the scenario is about proving compliance, maintaining compliance, consequences of failure, or privacy/data-handling responsibilities.

questions.q: A compliance dashboard is sent only to company executives and internal audit. Which reporting type is this?
questions.explanation: Internal compliance reporting communicates status to stakeholders inside the organization.

questions.q: A company submits required compliance evidence to a regulator. Which reporting type is this?
questions.explanation: External compliance reporting communicates required information to outside parties such as regulators.

questions.q: A security team reviews a vendor's security posture before signing a contract. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Due diligence is the investigation and evaluation performed before a decision.

questions.q: An organization discovers a known vulnerability and applies a reasonable protective control. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Due care means taking reasonable protective action after risks are known.

questions.q: An executive formally certifies that required controls are operating as stated. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Attestation is a formal certification or declaration.

questions.q: Employees click a button confirming they have read and understood the acceptable-use policy. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Acknowledgement confirms receipt or understanding of a policy or requirement.

questions.q: An external auditor independently confirms that certain compliance controls are functioning. Which type of attestation is this?
questions.explanation: External attestation is performed by an outside party.

questions.q: A tool continuously collects evidence that encryption settings remain compliant. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Automation can continuously test controls and collect compliance evidence.
